## Problem

PyNvVideoCodec has two failure modes:

- **Failed decode:** valid video -> unsupported video -> later valid videos fail because the decoder slot is poisoned.
- **Successful decode:** 720p -> 1080p -> 4K can grow the cached decoder. PyNvVideoCodec 2.2.3 may leak the replaced decoder until GPU memory is exhausted and all later videos fail.

## Fix

- Reject unsupported streams early with `GetDecoderCaps()` and retire failed slots.
- Size default decoders to the input; clamp configured `max_width`/`max_height` per codec and account for their retained surfaces.
- Keep routine rebuild cleanup stream-local; reserve device-wide recovery for failed requests.
- Decode 32 frames at a time, synchronizing and releasing each batch.

## Validation

Rebased onto `main` at `3fe917abb1`. On GB200 with PyTorch 26.06, Torch 2.13.0+cu130, and PyNvVideoCodec 2.0.4:

```bash
.venv-gpu/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/test_video.py -k pynvvideocodec -v
# 30 passed, 1 H100/H200-only skip

.venv-gpu/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/test_gpu_ipc_memory.py -v
# 18 passed
```

Full pre-commit passed on all changed files. Earlier GB200 Video-MME validation covered 10 videos x 2 passes, up to 256 frames, with stable GPU memory. Full 300-video H200 validation is pending.

No duplicate open PR was found. AI assistance was used; the human submitter is responsible for reviewing and validating the change.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Findings marked 🟡 are optional suggestions and need no follow-up push.

<!-- bhrv:fd2f9c069a0cbd18 -->

🔴 Operators get stale GPU-memory accounting for PyNvVideoCodec, risking CUDA OOM, since decoders now default to hardware-max surface sizes instead of actual video resolution. When max_width/max_height aren't configured (the default), _validate_decoder_caps (line 350) returns the GPU's hardware width_max/height_max, and PyNvVideoCodecDecoderSlot._construct (line 160-176) builds every decoder at those dimensions instead of the video's real resolution as before. PYNVVIDEOCODEC_DECODER_GPU_MEMORY_BYTES (line 60) is still a flat 128 MiB per decoder and is used by gpu_ipc_memory.py:198-224 to reserve KV-cache headroom. Fix: scale that reservation (or cap the default max dims) to the resolved max_width x max_height actually configured, not a stale flat constant.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger: any deployment using the PyNvVideoCodec backend without explicitly setting max_width/max_height (the default per vllm/multimodal/video_decoders/__init__.py:26-27), entering decode_frames_pynvvideocodec. In that path _validate_decoder_caps (pynvvideocodec.py:343-350) resolves the decoder's max dimensions to the GPU's hardware max rather than the video's actual resolution, and _construct (line 160) allocates decoder surfaces at that size for every slot. On base branch decoders were constructed/reconfigured without any max_width/max_height, so surfaces tracked actual stream size. gpu_ipc_memory.py:198-224 still reserves only PYNVVIDEOCODEC_DECODER_GPU_MEMORY_BYTES=128 MiB per decoder (pynvvideocodec.py:60), unchanged by this diff, so KV-cache sizing can under-reserve real decoder memory, risking CUDA OOM at runtime under concurrent high-resolution-capable hardware.

**Verification:** In `_validate_decoder_caps` (vllm/multimodal/video_decoders/pynvvideocodec.py:349-350), the default path returns hardware caps `width_max, height_max`, not the video's actual resolution. `_construct` (lines 160-182) passes these into `SimpleDecoder`, sizing the native frame pool at hardware max.

</details>

<!-- bhfn:1:normal -->

🔴 A single fixed max_width/max_height config can now make every video of a smaller-cap codec fail, even tiny ones, since GetDecoderCaps' width_max/height_max vary per codec/chroma/bit-depth but max_width/max_height is one global value (max_width/max_height is startup-only; request overrides are stripped in media/video.py:51-52). E.g. operator sets max_width=7680/max_height=4320 for HEVC, then every H.264 video (AVC caps typically 4096x4096) hits 'max_width > width_max' at pynvvideocodec.py:355 and raises 'Configured PyNvVideoCodec max_width and max_height are outside the hardware decoder limits' regardless of actual resolution. Fix: compare the video's own width/height against max_width/max_height clamped to that codec's width_max/height_max instead of rejecting whenever the global max exceeds this file's codec caps.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger: operator configures a single max_width/max_height (only possible at startup; VideoMediaIO.merge_kwargs strips request-level max_width/max_height, see vllm/multimodal/media/video.py:51-52) sized for one codec's hardware limits (e.g. HEVC 8192x8192), then a mixed-codec workload sends a video using a codec/profile with lower caps (e.g. AVC 4096x4096) through decode_frames_pynvvideocodec -> _validate_decoder_caps (pynvvideocodec.py:528). _validate_decoder_caps queries GetDecoderCaps per-file using that file's own GetNvCodecId/ChromaFormat/BitDepth (pynvvideocodec.py:327-331), so width_max/height_max differ by codec, but compares them against the one global max_width/max_height at line 353-359. Any video whose codec's width_max/height_max is below the configured max_width/max_height is rejected with 'outside the hardware decoder limits', even if the video itself is small and fully decodable. On the base branch there was no such per-codec caps check at all, so these videos decoded fine.

**Verification:** normal (conditional on operator config). The validation at vllm/multimodal/video_decoders/pynvvideocodec.py:352-363 compares a single global max_width/max_height against per-file-codec caps fetched via GetDecoderCaps (lines 327-332), which differ between codecs (AVC ~4096x4096 vs HEVC 8192x8192).

</details>

<!-- bhfn:1:normal -->

🟡 (optional) Every routine decoder rebuild now stalls all other PyNvVideoCodec slots on the GPU, not just actual decode failures. When reconfigure_decoder() fails for a new source (pynvvideocodec.py:200-205, an expected case per the comment at :203) or the request's max_width/max_height exceeds the slot's current size (:195-197), get_decoder() calls recover(), which runs decoder.stop(), gc.collect(), stream.synchronize(), then a device-wide torch.cuda.synchronize()+empty_cache(). On the base branch this same fallback only cleared self.decoder/self.source_path via the cheap invalidate() inside _construct(). Fix: scope routine rebuild cleanup to this slot's own stream, reserving the heavy device-wide drain for genuine failure recovery in _borrow_decoder_slot.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger: two consecutive decode requests land on the same PyNvVideoCodecDecoderSlot where the second source needs a rebuild, either because reconfigure_decoder() raises for an ordinary codec/profile/container change (comment at pynvvideocodec.py:203 calls this routine, not a failure) or because its max_width/max_height exceeds self.max_width/self.max_height (:195). get_decoder() (pynvvideocodec.py:196 and :204) now calls self.recover(), which does decoder.stop(), gc.collect(), self.stream.synchronize(), then torch.cuda.synchronize() and torch.cuda.empty_cache() for the whole device (pynvvideocodec.py:145-158). On the base branch (0f112d1) the identical fallback only called self.invalidate() inside _construct(), which just set self.decoder/self.source_path to None with no synchronization. With the default hw_decoders=2, a routine single-slot rebuild from mixed-codec traffic now blocks every other concurrently-decoding slot/stream on the GPU, where before it did not.

**Verification:** nit (performance/concurrency regression; nothing functionally breaks). recover() (pynvvideocodec.py:145-158) runs gc.collect(), self.stream.synchronize(), then a device-wide torch.cuda.synchronize() and torch.cuda.empty_cache(). get_decoder() now calls recover() on ordinary rebuilds: line 196 (max_width/max_height exceeds the slot's bounds) and line 204 (reconfigure_decoder() failure, treated at :203 as expected).

</details>

Addressed in afddaf7094. With no configured limit, the decoder is now sized to the source dimensions instead of the hardware maximum. Explicit max dimensions also scale the startup GPU-memory reservation using the configured retained RGB cache surfaces, with the existing 128 MiB reservation kept as the baseline. Added reservation coverage for an 8K configured ceiling.

Addressed in afddaf7094. Configured dimensions are now clamped to each stream codec/profile's decoder caps before the actual stream dimensions are checked, so a 7680x4320 workload ceiling no longer rejects a supported 1920x1080 H.264 input with 4096x4096 caps. Added a focused mixed-cap regression test.

Addressed in afddaf7094. Routine resolution growth and reconfigure fallback now use reset(), which drains only the slot's stream before rebuilding. The heavy gc/device-wide synchronize/empty-cache recovery remains only in _borrow_decoder_slot's failed-borrow path. Also replaced the new torch.cuda calls with torch.accelerator APIs.
left some comments, mostly around possible perf degradations in this PR

`gc.collect()` runs in the API-server process and holds the GIL for the whole collection, so it pauses the asyncio loop and the other renderer threads, i.e. streaming/tokenization for all requests, not just video ones. Its cost grows with the frontend heap. `recover()` is reachable by any input that passes the caps check but fails later (e.g. a truncated/corrupt bitstream), so a client can also trigger it repeatedly.

Is it needed given `decoder.stop()`, the `del decoder`s and the unchained re-raise? If a specific cycle keeps the native decoder alive, can we break it directly? If it is needed, could you share the measured pause on a realistic heap? The device sync + `empty_cache()` are fine by me: they only touch the frontend's own context and only on the failure path.

With the default (no configured bounds), `max_width`/`max_height` here are the source dims, so the slot is rebuilt at the new source's size rather than the union of old and new. Mixed orientations then rebuild on every alternation: 1920x1080 -> 1080x1920 (height grows) -> 1920x1080 (width grows) -> ... Each is a full `SimpleDecoder` construction, which is the cost slot reuse is meant to avoid, and phone-camera traffic mixes orientations a lot.

Suggestion: build at `max(self.max_width, max_width), max(self.max_height, max_height)`, subject to the same caps / `mb_num_max` clamping. For reference, 3840x3840 RGB x `PYNVVIDEOCODEC_DECODER_CACHE_SIZE` is ~88 MB, still under the 128 MiB per-decoder reservation.

This adds a second container parse to every request on the success path: `CreateDemuxer` here, then again inside `SimpleDecoder(...)` / `reconfigure_decoder()`. Do you have a number for this on a typical MP4 (especially larger files)? If it's noticeable, is there a cheaper way to get codec/chroma/bit depth/dims up front? The `GetDecoderCaps` result could also be memoized per `(codec, chroma, bit_depth)`.

Does `get_batch_frames_by_index` keep its decode position across calls with increasing indices, or does each call seek to the preceding keyframe independently? If the latter, every chunk boundary may re-decode part of a GOP. A main-vs-PR latency number for e.g. 256 frames from a long 1080p video would settle it.

The extra per-chunk `stream.synchronize()` itself looks cheap to me, since main didn't overlap decode with the D2H copy either.

Follow-up idea, not blocking: with chunked decode the device-side peak is roughly one chunk (decoder output + the `torch.stack` copy), but the lease still reserves `len(frame_idx) * H * W * 3`. Leasing per chunk (sized for the chunk's peak) would let more requests decode concurrently under the same `mm_ipc_gpu_memory_gb`. On main the peak was roughly 2x the leased bytes, so this PR already makes the accounting more honest.

🔴 Operators get stale GPU-memory accounting for PyNvVideoCodec, risking CUDA OOM, since decoders now default to hardware-max surface sizes instead of actual video resolution. When max_width/max_height aren't configured (the default), _validate_decoder_caps (line 350) returns the GPU's hardware width_max/height_max, and PyNvVideoCodecDecoderSlot._construct (line 160-176) builds every decoder at those dimensions instead of the video's real resolution as before. PYNVVIDEOCODEC_DECODER_GPU_MEMORY_BYTES (line 60) is still a flat 128 MiB per decoder and is used by gpu_ipc_memory.py:198-224 to reserve KV-cache headroom. Fix: scale that reservation (or cap the default max dims) to the resolved max_width x max_height actually configured, not a stale flat constant.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger: any deployment using the PyNvVideoCodec backend without explicitly setting max_width/max_height (the default per vllm/multimodal/video_decoders/__init__.py:26-27), entering decode_frames_pynvvideocodec. In that path _validate_decoder_caps (pynvvideocodec.py:343-350) resolves the decoder's max dimensions to the GPU's hardware max rather than the video's actual resolution, and _construct (line 160) allocates decoder surfaces at that size for every slot. On base branch decoders were constructed/reconfigured without any max_width/max_height, so surfaces tracked actual stream size. gpu_ipc_memory.py:198-224 still reserves only PYNVVIDEOCODEC_DECODER_GPU_MEMORY_BYTES=128 MiB per decoder (pynvvideocodec.py:60), unchanged by this diff, so KV-cache sizing can under-reserve real decoder memory, risking CUDA OOM at runtime under concurrent high-resolution-capable hardware.

**Verification:** In `_validate_decoder_caps` (vllm/multimodal/video_decoders/pynvvideocodec.py:349-350), the default path returns hardware caps `width_max, height_max`, not the video's actual resolution. `_construct` (lines 160-182) passes these into `SimpleDecoder`, sizing the native frame pool at hardware max.

</details>

<!-- bhfn:1:normal -->

🔴 A single fixed max_width/max_height config can now make every video of a smaller-cap codec fail, even tiny ones, since GetDecoderCaps' width_max/height_max vary per codec/chroma/bit-depth but max_width/max_height is one global value (max_width/max_height is startup-only; request overrides are stripped in media/video.py:51-52). E.g. operator sets max_width=7680/max_height=4320 for HEVC, then every H.264 video (AVC caps typically 4096x4096) hits 'max_width > width_max' at pynvvideocodec.py:355 and raises 'Configured PyNvVideoCodec max_width and max_height are outside the hardware decoder limits' regardless of actual resolution. Fix: compare the video's own width/height against max_width/max_height clamped to that codec's width_max/height_max instead of rejecting whenever the global max exceeds this file's codec caps.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger: operator configures a single max_width/max_height (only possible at startup; VideoMediaIO.merge_kwargs strips request-level max_width/max_height, see vllm/multimodal/media/video.py:51-52) sized for one codec's hardware limits (e.g. HEVC 8192x8192), then a mixed-codec workload sends a video using a codec/profile with lower caps (e.g. AVC 4096x4096) through decode_frames_pynvvideocodec -> _validate_decoder_caps (pynvvideocodec.py:528). _validate_decoder_caps queries GetDecoderCaps per-file using that file's own GetNvCodecId/ChromaFormat/BitDepth (pynvvideocodec.py:327-331), so width_max/height_max differ by codec, but compares them against the one global max_width/max_height at line 353-359. Any video whose codec's width_max/height_max is below the configured max_width/max_height is rejected with 'outside the hardware decoder limits', even if the video itself is small and fully decodable. On the base branch there was no such per-codec caps check at all, so these videos decoded fine.

**Verification:** normal (conditional on operator config). The validation at vllm/multimodal/video_decoders/pynvvideocodec.py:352-363 compares a single global max_width/max_height against per-file-codec caps fetched via GetDecoderCaps (lines 327-332), which differ between codecs (AVC ~4096x4096 vs HEVC 8192x8192).

</details>

<!-- bhfn:1:normal -->

🟡 (optional) Every routine decoder rebuild now stalls all other PyNvVideoCodec slots on the GPU, not just actual decode failures. When reconfigure_decoder() fails for a new source (pynvvideocodec.py:200-205, an expected case per the comment at :203) or the request's max_width/max_height exceeds the slot's current size (:195-197), get_decoder() calls recover(), which runs decoder.stop(), gc.collect(), stream.synchronize(), then a device-wide torch.cuda.synchronize()+empty_cache(). On the base branch this same fallback only cleared self.decoder/self.source_path via the cheap invalidate() inside _construct(). Fix: scope routine rebuild cleanup to this slot's own stream, reserving the heavy device-wide drain for genuine failure recovery in _borrow_decoder_slot.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger: two consecutive decode requests land on the same PyNvVideoCodecDecoderSlot where the second source needs a rebuild, either because reconfigure_decoder() raises for an ordinary codec/profile/container change (comment at pynvvideocodec.py:203 calls this routine, not a failure) or because its max_width/max_height exceeds self.max_width/self.max_height (:195). get_decoder() (pynvvideocodec.py:196 and :204) now calls self.recover(), which does decoder.stop(), gc.collect(), self.stream.synchronize(), then torch.cuda.synchronize() and torch.cuda.empty_cache() for the whole device (pynvvideocodec.py:145-158). On the base branch (0f112d1) the identical fallback only called self.invalidate() inside _construct(), which just set self.decoder/self.source_path to None with no synchronization. With the default hw_decoders=2, a routine single-slot rebuild from mixed-codec traffic now blocks every other concurrently-decoding slot/stream on the GPU, where before it did not.

**Verification:** nit (performance/concurrency regression; nothing functionally breaks). recover() (pynvvideocodec.py:145-158) runs gc.collect(), self.stream.synchronize(), then a device-wide torch.cuda.synchronize() and torch.cuda.empty_cache(). get_decoder() now calls recover() on ordinary rebuilds: line 196 (max_width/max_height exceeds the slot's bounds) and line 204 (reconfigure_decoder() failure, treated at :203 as expected).

</details>

<!-- bhfn:1:nit -->

Addressed in afddaf7094. With no configured limit, the decoder is now sized to the source dimensions instead of the hardware maximum. Explicit max dimensions also scale the startup GPU-memory reservation using the configured retained RGB cache surfaces, with the existing 128 MiB reservation kept as the baseline. Added reservation coverage for an 8K configured ceiling.

Addressed in afddaf7094. Configured dimensions are now clamped to each stream codec/profile's decoder caps before the actual stream dimensions are checked, so a 7680x4320 workload ceiling no longer rejects a supported 1920x1080 H.264 input with 4096x4096 caps. Added a focused mixed-cap regression test.

Addressed in afddaf7094. Routine resolution growth and reconfigure fallback now use reset(), which drains only the slot's stream before rebuilding. The heavy gc/device-wide synchronize/empty-cache recovery remains only in _borrow_decoder_slot's failed-borrow path. Also replaced the new torch.cuda calls with torch.accelerator APIs.

`gc.collect()` runs in the API-server process and holds the GIL for the whole collection, so it pauses the asyncio loop and the other renderer threads, i.e. streaming/tokenization for all requests, not just video ones. Its cost grows with the frontend heap. `recover()` is reachable by any input that passes the caps check but fails later (e.g. a truncated/corrupt bitstream), so a client can also trigger it repeatedly.

Is it needed given `decoder.stop()`, the `del decoder`s and the unchained re-raise? If a specific cycle keeps the native decoder alive, can we break it directly? If it is needed, could you share the measured pause on a realistic heap? The device sync + `empty_cache()` are fine by me: they only touch the frontend's own context and only on the failure path.

With the default (no configured bounds), `max_width`/`max_height` here are the source dims, so the slot is rebuilt at the new source's size rather than the union of old and new. Mixed orientations then rebuild on every alternation: 1920x1080 -> 1080x1920 (height grows) -> 1920x1080 (width grows) -> ... Each is a full `SimpleDecoder` construction, which is the cost slot reuse is meant to avoid, and phone-camera traffic mixes orientations a lot.

Suggestion: build at `max(self.max_width, max_width), max(self.max_height, max_height)`, subject to the same caps / `mb_num_max` clamping. For reference, 3840x3840 RGB x `PYNVVIDEOCODEC_DECODER_CACHE_SIZE` is ~88 MB, still under the 128 MiB per-decoder reservation.

This adds a second container parse to every request on the success path: `CreateDemuxer` here, then again inside `SimpleDecoder(...)` / `reconfigure_decoder()`. Do you have a number for this on a typical MP4 (especially larger files)? If it's noticeable, is there a cheaper way to get codec/chroma/bit depth/dims up front? The `GetDecoderCaps` result could also be memoized per `(codec, chroma, bit_depth)`.

Does `get_batch_frames_by_index` keep its decode position across calls with increasing indices, or does each call seek to the preceding keyframe independently? If the latter, every chunk boundary may re-decode part of a GOP. A main-vs-PR latency number for e.g. 256 frames from a long 1080p video would settle it.

The extra per-chunk `stream.synchronize()` itself looks cheap to me, since main didn't overlap decode with the D2H copy either.

Follow-up idea, not blocking: with chunked decode the device-side peak is roughly one chunk (decoder output + the `torch.stack` copy), but the lease still reserves `len(frame_idx) * H * W * 3`. Leasing per chunk (sized for the chunk's peak) would let more requests decode concurrently under the same `mm_ipc_gpu_memory_gb`. On main the peak was roughly 2x the leased bytes, so this PR already makes the accounting more honest.
